This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C No.12347/2019 on the file of XXXI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bangalore.
2. Notice issued to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through video conferencing and after identifying the same, the matter has been heard.
She is said to be staying in U.S, after re-marrying some other person, after divorce granted to this petitioner.

3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent-State.
4.
Based upon the Private Complaint of the respondent which was referred to the police and registered a case in crime No.310/2018 dated 14.06.2018 by Peenya Police Station.
The alleged offences filed against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 323, 324, 504, 506, 498A of IPC r/w Sections 3 & 4 of DP Act.
5. Learned counsel submits that during the pendency of the criminal proceedings, the parties have entered settlement between them in matrimonial case, M.C No.1596/2019.
Where the petitioner and respondents were settled their disputes and where the respondent undertaken to co-operate with the Court for closing the criminal case.
The mediation report is filed before this Court.
6. It is well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court

that once the matter has been settled between the parties in the Family Court and divorce has been granted, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Sri Sandesh vs V/S State Of Karnataka on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42902492/
